name: Dunbarton Rail Bridge
description: An old abandoned rail bridge. Although it was closed in 1982, you can just crawl under the fence and walk out onto the bridge. It's very pretty there and really cool to explore. The bridge has definitely seen better days. The bridge caught fire in 1998 and again in 2019, so be careful of the wooden ties. The surrounding area is weird (Fremont). The marsh has a strange odor and attracts a lot of flies and birds. People fish near the trailhead parking lot but I wouldn't eat anything caught there.

name: Centerville Flat Dispersed Campground
description:
Centerville Flat Dispersed Campground is a free, dispersed camping area offered by Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. The only amenities found here are vault toilets. There are no trash cans either. Otherwise this is strictly a designated boondocking area where camping is allowed anywhere.

name: Wentworth Springs Campground
description:
This is a free, developed campground offered by El Dorado National Forest strictly for high clearance, 4WD vehicles. There are eight (8) sites, all of which are designed for tent camping. The campground is only open from June to October. There are picnic tables, fire rings, and a vault toilet.
